{"consolidated_memory":"ml/serving/batcher.py - Four latency spike incidents (Feb-Jul 2026)

All incidents involved the same file (ml/serving/batcher.py, ml pipeline side) with the same signal pattern (tail far above the median in the serving histogram) and same repro (send mixed-size request trace), but different root causes, scopes, and outcomes.

INCIDENT 1: [2026-02-10]
- Scope: Only on staging read replica
- Root cause: An error swallowed by a bare except
- Fix: Narrowed the exception handler and let the failure propagate
- PR #3869, branch fix/latency-spike-1
- Result: Throughput rose 15 percent to 282 requests per second
- Note: Same corner of batcher.py as earlier latency spike work

INCIDENT 2: [2026-03-14]
- Scope: Only for accounts in the five percent rollout bucket
- Root cause: Two writes that were never wrapped in a transaction
- Fix: Wrapped both writes in one transaction
- PR #6637, branch fix/latency-spike-2
- Result: Error rate dropped from 3.0 percent to under 2 per ten thousand
- Test coverage: tests/ml/test_batcher.py
- Stack: Python

INCIDENT 3: [2026-05-26]
- Scope: Only for jobs scheduled across the midnight boundary
- Root cause: A race in lazy initialisation
- Fix: Guarded the init with a double-checked lock
- PR #6694, branch fix/latency-spike-3
- Result: Job finished in 39 minutes instead of 8 hours
- Test coverage: tests/ml/test_batcher.py
- Stack: Python

INCIDENT 4: [2026-07-03]
- Scope: Only for clients still pinned to the v1 SDK
- Root cause: Missing composite index on (tenant_id, created_at)
- Fix: Added the composite index and backfilled in batches
- PR #7335, branch fix/latency-spike-4
- Result: 85 duplicate rows a day stopped being written
- Test coverage: tests/ml/test_batcher.py
- Stack: Python"}
